title: Covariance risk, VaR and expected shortfall

objectives.text: Compute two-asset same-horizon portfolio variance with explicit covariance/correlation and valid positive-semidefinite input assumptions,without confusing volatility with tail loss.
Calculate an own empirical left-quantile VaR and quantile-integral expected shortfall including fractional boundary mass/ties,stating loss sign,horizon,scenario weights and sample limitations.

blocks.markdown: For same-horizon return vector R,weights w,and covariance Sigma,Var(w^T R)=w^T Sigmaw. With two assets and weights(w,1-w),variance=w²*sigma1²+(1-w)²*sigma2²+2w(1-w)*sigma1*sigma2*rho. Volatilities are standard deviations in DECIMAL return units over the same horizon;variance is squared return units. Correlation matters,so portfolio volatility is not generally a weighted average of individual volatilities. Positive-semidefinite covariance is required;arbitrary pairwise correlations in larger matrices can be jointly invalid.

blocks.title: Variance is not a tail-loss forecast

steps.text: Equal weights,sigma1=0.2,sigma2=0.3,rho0give variance0.25*0.04+0.25*0.09=0.0325,volatility sqrt(0.0325)≈0.180278. This is return dispersion,not a currency loss threshold.
At rho1,variance=(0.5*0.2+0.5*0.3)^2=0.0625. At rho-1with equal vol0.2and equal weights,variance0under this exact two-factor model. Neither correlation is a promise about future assets.

Mapping returns to portfolio currency PnL requires positions/notional,pricing/nonlinearity and horizon conventions. Option portfolios may need full revaluation/scenarios rather than one fixed linear covariance approximation.

blocks.caption: Expected0.032500;0.0;0.062500. Own exact-float interface weights0..1,vols0..2,correlation[-1,1]. A two-factor sum-of-squares decomposition preserves nonnegative variance for this two-asset domain without a blanket max(variance,0)that would hide invalid larger covariance matrices. It does not estimate covariance,annualize data or implement leveraged portfolios.

blocks.markdown: Define loss L=-PnL,so larger is worse,and name horizon,currency,valuation model and scenario probabilities. Own left quantile VaR_alpha=inf{x:F_L(x)>=alpha}. It is a threshold,not maximum possible loss and not the mean loss beyond it. Quantile software interpolation conventions differ;the code uses the left quantile of the equal-weight empirical distribution,not an unlabelled library default. Negative VaR is allowed when even that quantile is a gain;do not silently floor it to0without saying the risk policy changed.

Use ES_alpha=(1/(1-alpha))*integral_alpha^1 Q_L(u)du,where Q_Lis that left quantile. For finite equal-weight scenarios,take exactly the worst n*(1-alpha)scenario units,including fractional boundary weight,then average over that tail mass. This handles atoms/ties. E[L|L>VaR]or E[L|L>=VaR]can differ from this ESwhen there is probability mass at VaR;do not call either conditional average universally equivalent. BIS terminology is a high-level description;the detailed sample convention here is explicit.

blocks.title: Fractional mass and a tied quantile

steps.text: Losses[0,10,20],alpha0.5. Left VaR10. Worst tail is1.5scenario units:all20plus half of10. ES=(20+0.5*10)/1.5=50/3,not20and not the unweighted average15.
Losses[0,10,10,20],alpha0.5. Left VaR10and worst2units are20and10,ES15. Averaging only losses strictly>VaRgives20and overstates this defined tail average.
Losses[-5,-2,-1],alpha0.5have VaR-2,ES-4/3. These are negative losses,gains under our sign convention. No floor is applied. All calculations describe only this declared finite scenario distribution.

blocks.source:
from fractions import Fraction as F

def empirical_tail(losses,alpha):
    # Equal scenario masses,positive loss means bad;left quantile convention.
    if type(losses) is not list or not 1<=len(losses)<=100:
        raise ValueError("invalid bounded scenario list")
    if any(type(x) is not int or not -1000000<=x<=1000000 for x in losses):
        raise ValueError("invalid exact loss")
    if type(alpha) is not F or not 0<alpha<1:
        raise ValueError("invalid confidence level")
    ordered=sorted(losses)
    n=len(ordered)
    index=(alpha.numerator*n+alpha.denominator-1)//alpha.denominator-1
    var=F(ordered[index])
    mass=F(n)*(1-alpha) # tail measured in equal-scenario units
    remaining=mass
    total=F(0)
    for loss in reversed(ordered):
        take=min(F(1),remaining)
        total+=take*loss
        remaining-=take
        if remaining==0:break
    return var,total/mass

print(empirical_tail([0,10,20],F(1,2)))
print(empirical_tail([0,10,10,20],F(1,2)))
print(empirical_tail([-5,-2,-1],F(1,2)))

blocks.markdown: A low historical VaR/EScan reflect missing crisis scenarios,short samples,stale positions,wrong correlations,liquidity/impact/credit omissions or regime change. ESlooks deeper into modeled tails than VaR,but rare-tail estimation is noisy and neither statistic is a worst-case guarantee. Stress tests specify additional adverse scenarios;they do not magically supply calibrated probabilities. Report horizon,confidence,loss convention,weights,window/scenario coverage and valuation assumptions alongside the number. Do not sqrt-time-scale tails/covariance without the needed temporal assumptions.

Independent transfer:build empirical CDFquantile intervals of width1/nand integrate their overlap with(alpha,1]exactly;compare with the worst-mass algorithm across small enumerated loss lists and rational confidence levels. Test ties,all-equal,all-gain,confidence near0or1,fractional mass,input permutation and translation/positive scale. For covariance,compare with direct quadratic form and enumerated two-factor scenarios. Then explain why a larger correlation matrix needs a full PSDcheck and why model risk is separate from exact sample arithmetic.

Sources:[Columbia portfolio variance/correlation lecture](https://www.columbia.edu/~amm26/lecture%20files/marketEquilibriumRelativeRisk.pdf),[BISmarket-risk terminology](https://www.bis.org/committees/bcbs/basel-framework/standard/mar/10/inforce/2023-01-01/published/2020-03-27),[Acerbi/Tasche expected-shortfall paper hosted as BISconsultation response](https://www.bis.org/2026-07/acertasc.pdf). The last source is an authored research/consultation contribution,not BISpolicy. It uses lower-tail PnL and tail-probability alpha;our upper-loss/confidence convention is explicitly transformed. No regulatory capital-compliance claim is made.

summary: Portfolio covariance includes cross terms and depends on horizon/valid inputs. VaR is a declared loss quantile,not maximum loss;ESaverages exact worst tail mass,including ties/fractional boundaries. Exact empirical arithmetic does not establish real future tail coverage or regulatory readiness.
